title: Conditions Have No Good or Bad
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Question: The Fourth Patriarch instructed Farong, saying: “Conditions have no good or bad; good and bad arise from the mind.” But conditions clearly have good and bad. For example, if your body is healthy, that is good; if you fall ill, even to the point of death, that is bad. This is an objective fact—how can it arise from the mind?

inline.s: Conditions have no good or bad; good and bad arise from the mind.
If the mind does not force names upon them, from whence do false feelings arise?
Since false feelings no longer arise, the true mind freely knows all.
Question: The Fourth Patriarch instructed Farong, saying:
“Conditions have no good or bad
(conditions have no good or bad)
; good and bad arise from the mind.”
But conditions clearly have good and bad. For example, if your body is healthy, that is good; if you fall ill, even gravely, that is bad. This is an objective fact—where does it arise from the mind?

Answer: You are looking at conditions from a worldly viewpoint, supposing them to be real, and therefore good and bad are objective facts. But from the viewpoint of the Buddhadharma, which sees through to the truth of the universe, conditions are illusory forms, like things in a dream. The reason beings revolve in the cycle of birth and death without end is that they take conditions for real. Even some who study Buddhism know that conditions are illusory, yet the moment conditions bear upon their own fortunes they at once take them as real—this is the ingrained habit from beginningless kalpas of
false attachment
(taking the illusory for real).
For example,
Ambapali asked Manjushri: ‘You clearly know that birth is a Dharma of the unborn; why then are you carried along by birth and death?’ Manjushri replied: ‘Because one’s power is not yet complete.’

(Translation: Ambapali asked Bodhisattva Manjushri: ‘Clearly knowing that birth is the unborn Dharma, why are you still turned about by birth and death?’ Bodhisattva Manjushri answered: ‘Because the power to still false attachment is not yet sufficient.’ See in detail
“A Discussion of Life and Death”,
.) Therefore, practice consists in purifying the habit of false attachment in order to end birth and death. The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment says:
“Knowing illusion, one leaves it at once, without need of expedient means; leaving illusion, one is awakened, with no degrees of progression.”
(For its commentary, see
the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment Explained,
Therefore, in practice, one must, with feet planted on the ground, leave illusion. For example, you certainly know
“all marks are all false and vain”
this well-known phrase, and you believe this supreme truth in the Diamond Sutra. Since all marks (including conditions) are illusory, how can there be any good or bad? Therefore the Heart Sutra says:
“These dharmas are all empty marks, neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, neither increasing nor decreasing.”
(For its commentary, see
the Heart Sutra Explained,
.) But when you ponder “conditions have no good or bad; good and bad arise from the mind,” you forget
“all marks are all false and vain”

. Then you take conditions to be real and think good and bad are objective facts. Why is this so? It is the ingrained habit of false attachment. This is not to blame you, for this is a quite common situation. That you are able to earnestly ponder
“conditions have no good or bad; good and bad arise from the mind”
shows that you are earnestly practicing. When you have understood
“conditions have no good or bad; good and bad arise from the mind”
the principle in it, then apply it whenever you touch conditions:
“Knowing illusion, one leaves it at once, without need of expedient means; leaving illusion, one is awakened, with no degrees of progression.”
This is listening, pondering, and cultivating.
As for your saying “if the body is healthy, that is good; if you fall ill, even gravely, that is bad”—I suggest you read
“A Discussion of Life and Death”,
Once you get the principle in it clear, and then gradually realize and apply it, it will be a great help to escaping suffering.
